I attempt to relay most of the plot, as well as any information regarding character development/factoids.

**s6e5 Tanks for Nuthin'**

Dr. Mrs. The Monarch pressures Monarch to start arching someone else as she currently views him as a shiftless layabout. She leaves the house to investigate Haranguetan's death, as the Blue Morpho has been dead for several years. We learn that there are 9 more supervillains in line for Venture arching rights, so the two get to work getting the Morpho Mobile out of the impound lot. At the impound lot, the duo solidify their role as "vigilantes" when the Blue Morpho darts one of the officers.

Dr. Mrs. The Monarch's investigation leads us to Haranguetan's Widow, Battleaxe, who takes the Haranguetank from the impound lot on a vengeful warpath to Venture Tower, losing control on arrival and crashing into the same hole Haranguetan fell into, and taking Villain Think Tank with her. The crash resulted in their death. While helping Battleaxe get the Haranguetank, Dr. Mrs. The Monarch spots Blue Morpho from a distance. That, with the surveillance footage of Haranguetan's death provided by Wide Wale, leads Dr. Mrs. The monarch to believe that Rusty Venture is the Blue Morpho.

Brock's sexual encounter with Warriana and her unwillingness to reciprocate morning conversation leaves him confused and possibly experiencing anal leakage. Perhaps for the first time in his life, the roles seem to have been reversed.

Dwight video taped Billy intoxicated from the God Gas ala https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9cpbENgsXqM and put it online resulting in a PR disaster for Venture Tech Industries. Ghost Pirate Captain goes into PR mode to keep the Venture stock from falling further, during which we may have learned the alter ego to Warriana: a WWNews anchor by the only given name so far "Ms. Warrington" (who has an atrocious accent).

We meet Dean's philosophy instructor, Professor Nidaba (villain name Think Tank), next in line with arching rights after Haranguetan. A man with sherlock-like deduction skills, a head larger than his body, and confined to a hover chair. Though a villain, he warns Dean to not be home that night, but doesn't tell him it's because he was planning an arch. Think Tank attacks in a tank body with a large single barrel high velocity cannon and a force field. Initially, it is revealed that he simply desires a challenging game of chess from a worthy mind. Venture declines and decides to register a complaint with the Guild while Brock intervenes. Think Tank is defeated with help from Warriana, who clears the air with Brock. It appears the two are officially dating, though it is not clear the boundaries of this relationship.

During Think Tank's assault on Venture Tower, we see a list of known aliases for Brock Samson: Goldilocks, Jesus TralFaz (http://www.urbandictionary.com/define.php?term=Tralfaz ?), Ape Drape, Captain Mullethead, Frankenmullet, Brock of Ages, Thinkulese, Brock Lobster, Brocodile, Pop 'n' Fresh, Babe Ruthless, Brock Ness Monster, Agent Topanga Lawrence, Hockey Hair
